head: Booking.com scam on WhatsApp uses real booking details to demand payment
dek: Scammers are messaging travellers on WhatsApp with their real names, emails and hotel details, claiming to be Booking.com or Expedia and demanding a quick payment through a link or the booking gets cancelled. New Zealand's Travel Agents Association says it's happening daily.
details: The NZ Herald reports cases where the payment request came in an unexpected currency, such as euros for a Copenhagen stay, and one where a traveller got 24 hours to pay. Booking.com had a data breach in April, Expedia Group is investigating a cyber attack it says came through a third-party provider, and New Zealand booking site Bookit says it was hacked in early November. Netsafe says the scams involve many travel and accommodation sites, not just one.
where: Reported in New Zealand; travellers using Booking.com, Expedia and other booking sites
means: If a message knows your booking, that doesn't make it real: your details may have leaked, and a payment outside the booking app can be lost for good.
todo: Don't pay through a link sent on WhatsApp or by email. Open your original booking confirmation or the booking app to check, look for odd web addresses, spelling mistakes or a different currency, and don't let a deadline rush you.
